extracted.intended_audience: faculty and researchers preparing external grant proposals (university)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing external research grant proposals, focusing on common reasons for rejection and how to make proposals clear, appropriately targeted, and competitive. Useful for faculty, staff, and graduate students seeking sponsored research funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catch the reviewer's attention
rubrics_metrics.description: The document that does not catch the attention of the reader cannot compete on the more formal criteria associated with quality of design and congruence with the agency’s priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because reviewers read many proposals, the proposal must stand out early; craft a compelling abstract and introduction that project the unique or attractive elements of your research question or approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong abstract and introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract and introduction sections are very important, since they must project whatever unique or attractive elements are contained in your research question or approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these sections to highlight novelty, significance, and intriguing aspects of the project so reviewers notice and continue reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet the submission deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadline for submission was not met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission is fundamental; missing a deadline is an automatic or frequent cause of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate topic for the funding agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal topic was not appropriate to the funding agency to which it was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the research aligns with the agency’s mission, program priorities, and current solicitations before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow guidelines for content, format, and length exactly
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for proposal content, format, and/or length were not followed exactly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere precisely to all stated requirements (page limits, margins, font, required sections). Noncompliance signals carelessness and can lead to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal lacks novelty or intriguing elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed question, design, and method were completely traditional, with nothing that could strike a reviewer as unusual, intriguing, or clever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate innovation or an original angle; purely routine or incremental proposals are less competitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not a current agency priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed area of study was not an agency priority for this year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check current program solicitations and priorities; a good project may still be rejected if it doesn't fit current funding emphases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of clarity in describing study elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal was not absolutely clear in describing one or more elements of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about aims, hypotheses, procedures, analyses, and expected outcomes; ambiguity undermines reviewer confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of completeness in describing study elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal was not absolutely complete in describing one or more elements of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all necessary components (methods details, timelines, personnel roles, resources) so reviewers can assess feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient literature review / unfamiliarity with field
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors' review of the literature indicated they did not know the territory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate command of relevant literature; situate your work within current knowledge and explain how it advances the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project beyond investigators' capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed study appeared to be beyond the capacity of the authors in terms of training, experience, and available resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match project scope to team expertise and institutional support; document relevant experience and resource availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method unsuited to research purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed method of study was unsuited to the purpose of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose methods that directly address your research questions and justify methodological choices, including limitations and alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unrealistic budget estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: The budget was unrealistic in terms of estimated requirements for equipment, supplies, and personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare realistic, well-justified budgets; reviewers and program officers judge feasibility partly by how credible the budget is.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs outweigh potential benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of the proposed project appeared to be greater than any possible benefit to be derived from its completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proposed budget and requested resources are proportional to the expected scientific or societal gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highly partisan positions that alienate reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors took highly partisan positions on issues, and thus became vulnerable to the prejudices of the reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overly partisan framing; present arguments and interpretations objectively to reduce bias risks among diverse reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor quality of writing
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of writing was poor (e.g., sweeping and grandiose claims, convoluted reasoning, excessive repetitions, or unreasonable length).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write clearly and concisely, avoid exaggerated claims, organize arguments logically, remove redundancies, and respect length limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical defects and carelessness
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal contained an unreasonable number of mechanical defects that reflected carelessness and the author’s unwillingness to attend to detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofread carefully for typos, formatting errors, and inconsistencies; many small defects signal a lack of rigor and raise concerns about project execution.
